NASB.1: And it came about in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
NASB.2: [that] they made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).
NASB.3: All these came as allies to the valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea).
NASB.4: Twelve years they had served Chedorlaomer, but the thirteenth year they rebelled.
NASB.5: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings that were with him, came and defeated the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim and the Zuzim in Ham and the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
NASB.6: and the Horites in their Mount Seir, as far as El-paran, which is by the wilderness.
NASB.7: Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and conquered all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
NASB.8: And the king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah and the king of Admah and the king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) came out; and they arrayed for battle against them in the valley of Siddim,
NASB.9: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam and Tidal king of Goiim and Amraphel king of Shinar and Arioch king of Ellasar-- four kings against five.
NASB.10: Now the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and they fell into them. But those who survived fled to the hill country.
NASB.11: Then they took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food supply, and departed.
NASB.12: They also took Lot, Abram's nephew, and his possessions and departed, for he was living in Sodom.
NASB.13: Then a fugitive came and told Abram the Hebrew. Now he was living by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner, and these were allies with Abram.
NASB.14: When Abram heard that his relative had been taken captive, he led out his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and went in pursuit as far as Dan.
NASB.15: He divided his forces against them by night, he and his servants, and defeated them, and pursued them as far as Hobah, which is north of Damascus.
NASB.16: He brought back all the goods, and also brought back his relative Lot with his possessions, and also the women, and the people.
NASB.17: Then after his return from the defeat of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him at the valley of Shaveh (that is, the King's Valley).
NASB.18: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; now he was a priest of God Most High.
NASB.19: He blessed him and said, 'Blessed be Abram of God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth;
NASB.20: And blessed be God Most High, Who has delivered your enemies into your hand.' He gave him a tenth of all.
NASB.21: The king of Sodom said to Abram, 'Give the people to me and take the goods for yourself.'
NASB.22: Abram said to the king of Sodom, 'I have sworn to the LORD God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth,
NASB.23: that I will not take a thread or a sandal thong or anything that is yours, for fear you would say, 'I have made Abram rich.'
NASB.24: 'I will take nothing except what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; let them take their share.'

NKJV.1: And it came to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of nations,
NKJV.2: that they made war with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).
NKJV.3: All these joined together in the Valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea).
NKJV.4: Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
NKJV.5: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings that were with him came and attacked the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
NKJV.6: and the Horites in their mountain of Seir, as far as El Paran, which is by the wilderness.
NKJV.7: Then they turned back and came to En Mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and attacked all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who dwelt in Hazezon Tamar.
NKJV.8: And the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) went out and joined together in battle in the Valley of Siddim
NKJV.9: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of nations, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against five.
NKJV.10: Now the Valley of Siddim was full of asphalt pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled; some fell there, and the remainder fled to the mountains.
NKJV.11: Then they took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their provisions, and went their way.
NKJV.12: They also took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son who dwelt in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.
NKJV.13: Then one who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew, for he dwelt by the terebinth trees of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner; and they were allies with Abram.
NKJV.14: Now when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his three hundred and eighteen trained servants who were born in his own house, and went in pursuit as far as Dan.
NKJV.15: He divided his forces against them by night, and he and his servants attacked them and pursued them as far as Hobah, which is north of Damascus.
NKJV.16: So he brought back all the goods, and also brought back his brother Lot and his goods, as well as the women and the people.
NKJV.17: And the king of Sodom went out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh (that is, the King’s Valley), after his return from the defeat of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him.
NKJV.18: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was the priest of God Most High.
NKJV.19: And he blessed him and said:  “Blessed be Abram of God Most High,  Possessor of heaven and earth;
NKJV.20: And blessed be God Most High, Who has delivered your enemies into your hand.”  And he gave him a tithe of all.
NKJV.21: Now the king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the persons, and take the goods for yourself.”
NKJV.22: But Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have raised my hand to the LORD, God Most High, the Possessor of heaven and earth,
NKJV.23: that I will take nothing, from a thread to a sandal strap, and that I will not take anything that is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich’—
NKJV.24: except only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; let them take their portion.”

ESV.1: In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
ESV.2: these kings made war with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).
ESV.3: And all these joined forces in the Valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea).
ESV.4: Twelve years they had served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
ESV.5: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him came and defeated the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
ESV.6: and the Horites in their hill country of Seir as far as El-paran on the border of the wilderness.
ESV.7: Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh) and defeated all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who were dwelling in Hazazon-tamar.
ESV.8: Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) went out, and they joined battle in the Valley of Siddim
ESV.9: with Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar, four kings against five.
ESV.10: Now the Valley of Siddim was full of bitumen pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some fell into them, and the rest fled to the hill country.
ESV.11: So the enemy took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their provisions, and went their way.
ESV.12: They also took Lot, the son of Abram's brother, who was dwelling in Sodom, and his possessions, and went their way.
ESV.13: Then one who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew, who was living by the oaks  of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and of Aner. These were allies of Abram.
ESV.14: When Abram heard that his kinsman had been taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, 318 of them, and went in pursuit as far as Dan.
ESV.15: And he divided his forces against them by night, he and his servants, and defeated them and pursued them to Hobah, north of Damascus.
ESV.16: Then he brought back all the possessions, and also brought back his kinsman Lot with his possessions, and the women and the people.
ESV.17: After his return from the defeat of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh (that is, the King's Valley).
ESV.18: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. (He was priest of God Most High.)
ESV.19: And he blessed him and said, “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Possessor  of heaven and earth;
ESV.20: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand!”  And Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
ESV.21: And the king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the persons, but take the goods for yourself.”
ESV.22: But Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have lifted my hand  to the LORD, God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth,
ESV.23: that I would not take a thread or a sandal strap or anything that is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’
ESV.24: I will take nothing but what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me. Let Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre take their share.”

WEB.1: In the days of Amraphel, king of Shinar, Arioch, king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, and Tidal, king of Goiim,
WEB.2: they made war with Bera, king of Sodom, and with Birsha, king of Gomorrah, Shinab, king of Admah, and Shemeber, king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (also called Zoar).
WEB.3: All these joined together in the valley of Siddim (also called the Salt Sea).
WEB.4: They served Chedorlaomer for twelve years, and in the thirteenth year, they rebelled.
WEB.5: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer came, and the kings who were with him, and struck the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
WEB.6: and the Horites in their Mount Seir, to El Paran, which is by the wilderness.
WEB.7: They returned, and came to En Mishpat (also called Kadesh), and struck all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that lived in Hazazon Tamar.
WEB.8: The king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (also called Zoar) went out; and they set the battle in array against them in the valley of Siddim;
WEB.9: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings against the five.
WEB.10: Now the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and some fell there, and those who remained fled to the hills.
WEB.11: They took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their food, and went their way.
WEB.12: They took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who lived in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.
WEB.13: One who had escaped came and told Abram, the Hebrew. At that time, he lived by the oaks of Mamre, the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner; and they were allies of Abram.
WEB.14: When Abram heard that his relative was taken captive, he led out his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.
WEB.15: He divided himself against them by night, he and his servants, and struck them, and pursued them to Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.
WEB.16: He brought back all the goods, and also brought back his relative, Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the other people.
WEB.17: The king of Sodom went out to meet him after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, at the valley of Shaveh (that is, the King’s Valley).
WEB.18: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine: and he was priest of God Most High.
WEB.19: He blessed him, and said, “Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth:
WEB.20: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Abram gave him a tenth of all.
WEB.21: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself.”
WEB.22: Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have lifted up my hand to Yahweh, God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth,
WEB.23: that I will not take a thread nor a sandal strap nor anything that is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’
WEB.24: I will accept nothing from you except that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their portion.”

AMP.1: In the days of the [Eastern] kings Amraphel of Shinar, Arioch of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer of Elam, and Tidal of Goiim,
AMP.2: they [invaded the Jordan Valley near the Dead Sea, and] made war with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela(that is, Zoar).
AMP.3: All of these [kings] joined together [as allies] in the Valley of Siddim (that is, the Sea of Salt).
AMP.4: Twelve years they had served Chedorlaomer [the most powerful king in the invading confederacy], but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
AMP.5: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the [three] kings who were with him attacked and subdued the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
AMP.6: and the Horites in their mountainous country of Seir, as far as El-paran, which is on the border of the wilderness.
AMP.7: Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and subdued all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
AMP.8: Then the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela (that is, Zoar) came out; and they joined together for battle with the invading kings in the Valley of Siddim,
AMP.9: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam and Tidal king of Goiim and Amraphel king of Shinar and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against five.
AMP.10: Now the Valley of Siddim was full of tar (bitumen) pits; and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, they fell into them. But the remainder [of the kings] who survived fled to the hill country.
AMP.11: Then the victors took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food supply and provisions and left.
AMP.12: And they also took [captive] Lot, Abram's nephew, and his possessions and left, for he was living in Sodom.
AMP.13: Then a survivor who had escaped [from the invading forces on the other side of the Jordan] came and told Abram the Hebrew. Now he was living by the terebinths (oaks) of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner—they were allies of Abram.
AMP.14: When Abram heard that his nephew [Lot] had been captured, he armed and led out his trained men, born in his own house, [numbering] three hundred and eighteen, and went in pursuit as far [north] as Dan.
AMP.15: He divided his forces against them by night, he and his servants, and attacked and defeated them, and pursued them as far as Hobah, which is north of Damascus.
AMP.16: And he brought back all the goods, and also brought back his nephew Lot and his possessions, and also the women, and the people.
AMP.17: Then after Abram's return from the defeat (slaughter) of Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh (that is, the King's Valley).
AMP.18: Melchizedek king of Salem (ancient Jerusalem) brought out bread and wine [for them]; he was the priest of God Most High.
AMP.19:
And Melchizedek blessed Abram and said,
"Blessed (joyful, favored) be Abram by God Most High,
Creator and Possessor of heaven and earth;

CSB17.1: In those days King Amraphel of Shinar, <sup>ⓒ</sup> King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, <sup>ⓓ</sup> and King Tidal of Goiim <sup>[1]</sup>
CSB17.2: waged war against King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, and King Shemeber of Zeboiim, <sup>ⓔ</sup> as well as the king of Bela (that is, Zoar <sup>ⓕ</sup>).
CSB17.3: All of these came as allies to the Siddim Valley (that is, the Dead Sea <sup>ⓖ</sup>).
CSB17.4: They were subject to Chedorlaomer for twelve years, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
CSB17.5: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him came and defeated the Rephaim <sup>ⓗ</sup> in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, <sup>ⓘ</sup> the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
CSB17.6: and the Horites <sup>ⓙ</sup> in the mountains of Seir, as far as El-paran <sup>ⓚ</sup> by the wilderness.
CSB17.7: Then they came back to invade En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh <sup>ⓛ</sup>), and they defeated the whole territory of the Amalekites, as well as the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.8: Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) went out and lined up for battle in the Siddim Valley
CSB17.9: against King Chedorlaomer of Elam, King Tidal of Goiim, King Amraphel of Shinar, and King Arioch of Ellasar — four kings against five.
CSB17.10: Now the Siddim Valley contained many asphalt pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some fell into them, <sup>[2]</sup> but the rest fled to the mountains. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.11: The four kings took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food and went on.
CSB17.12: They also took Abram’s nephew Lot and his possessions, for he was living in Sodom, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and they went on.
CSB17.13: One of the survivors came and told Abram the Hebrew, <sup>ⓑ</sup> who lived near the oaks belonging to Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and the brother of Aner. They were bound by a treaty with <sup>[3]</sup> Abram.
CSB17.14: When Abram heard that his relative had been taken prisoner, he assembled <sup>[4]</sup> his 318 trained men, born in his household, <sup>ⓒ</sup> and they went in pursuit as far as Dan. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.15: And he and his servants deployed against them by night, defeated them, and pursued them as far as Hobah to the north of Damascus.
CSB17.16: He brought back all the goods and also his relative Lot and his goods, as well as the women and the other people.
CSB17.17: After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him in the Shaveh Valley (that is, the King’s Valley <sup>ⓔ</sup>).
CSB17.18: Melchizedek, king of Salem, <sup>[5]</sup> <sup>ⓕ</sup> brought out bread and wine; he was a priest to God Most High. <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.19:
He blessed him and said: Abram is blessed by God Most High,
Creator [6] of heaven and earth,
CSB17.20:
and blessed be God Most High
who has handed over your enemies to you.
And Abram gave him a tenth of everything. ⓗ
CSB17.21: Then the king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, but take the possessions for yourself.”
CSB17.22: But Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have raised my hand in an oath to the LORD, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
CSB17.23: that I will not take a thread or sandal strap or anything that belongs to you, so you can never say, ‘I made Abram rich.’
CSB17.24: I will take nothing <sup>[7]</sup> except what the servants have eaten. But as for the share of the men who came with me — Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre — they can take their share.”

NLT.1: About this time war broke out in the region. King Amraphel of Babylonia, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Kedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim
NLT.2: fought against King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (also called Zoar).
NLT.3: This second group of kings joined forces in Siddim Valley (that is, the valley of the Dead Sea ).
NLT.4: For twelve years they had been subject to King Kedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled against him.
NLT.5: One year later Kedorlaomer and his allies arrived and defeated the Rephaites at Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites at Ham, the Emites at Shaveh-kiriathaim,
NLT.6: and the Horites at Mount Seir, as far as El-paran at the edge of the wilderness.
NLT.7: Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat (now called Kadesh) and conquered all the territory of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites living in Hazazon-tamar.
NLT.8: Then the rebel kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela (also called Zoar) prepared for battle in the valley of the Dead Sea.
NLT.9: They fought against King Kedorlaomer of Elam, King Tidal of Goiim, King Amraphel of Babylonia, and King Arioch of Ellasar — four kings against five.
NLT.10: As it happened, the valley of the Dead Sea was filled with tar pits. And as the army of the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some fell into the tar pits, while the rest escaped into the mountains.
NLT.11: The victorious invaders then plundered Sodom and Gomorrah and headed for home, taking with them all the spoils of war and the food supplies.
NLT.12: They also captured Lot — Abram’s nephew who lived in Sodom — and carried off everything he owned.
NLT.13: But one of Lot’s men escaped and reported everything to Abram the Hebrew, who was living near the oak grove belonging to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his relatives, Eshcol and Aner, were Abram’s allies.
NLT.14: When Abram heard that his nephew Lot had been captured, he mobilized the 318 trained men who had been born into his household. Then he pursued Kedorlaomer’s army until he caught up with them at Dan.
NLT.15: There he divided his men and attacked during the night. Kedorlaomer’s army fled, but Abram chased them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
NLT.16: Abram recovered all the goods that had been taken, and he brought back his nephew Lot with his possessions and all the women and other captives.
NLT.17: After Abram returned from his victory over Kedorlaomer and all his allies, the king of Sodom went out to meet him in the valley of Shaveh (that is, the King’s Valley).
NLT.18: And Melchizedek, the king of Salem and a priest of God Most High, brought Abram some bread and wine.
NLT.19:
Melchizedek blessed Abram with this blessing: “Blessed be Abram by God Most High,
Creator of heaven and earth.
NLT.20:
And blessed be God Most High,
who has defeated your enemies for you.”
Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of all the goods he had recovered.
NLT.21: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give back my people who were captured. But you may keep for yourself all the goods you have recovered.”
NLT.22: Abram replied to the king of Sodom, “I solemnly swear to the LORD, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
NLT.23: that I will not take so much as a single thread or sandal thong from what belongs to you. Otherwise you might say, ‘I am the one who made Abram rich.’
NLT.24: I will accept only what my young warriors have already eaten, and I request that you give a fair share of the goods to my allies — Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre.”
